# NOTES ON SETTINGS:

- negative prompts dont work for cfg 1. increasing cfg exponentially increases time taken to finish and wont always work well with speed-up loras.

- if you have a good result then fix the seed, disable the speed-up lora, set cfg to 2.5 and steps to 20. try again. It improves quality at the cost of speed (about 2 to 4 times slower).

Choose your preferred speed-up lora and set the steps in the sampler accordingly.
I use 8 or 4 steps speed-up loras with cfg 1. Then you can disable the speed-up lora, fix the seed, and push for 20 steps in sampler with higher cfg (2.5) settings for improved final result.

MARKDKBERRY.com

Depending on your needs, this is good or bad. If I use it to make characters with portraits very good, if I use it to swap people into complex shots with multiple people or distances, it has a lot more challenges.

So my use case for this is dual purpose:

1. **DEVELOPING CHARACTERS ANGLES FROM A SINGLE IMAGE PORTRAIT SHOT**: 

- I rotate faces in portrait looking for high character consistency using one original image, and prompting for different angles. When it hits the spot I disable the speed-up lora, fix the seed, and run 20 steps with cfg 2.5 trying to get rid of the plastic look, while enhancing the consistency. Time is increased (x4 sometimes) but results are more accurate to original image.
     + note that each new face angle needs a different seed to keep consistency quite often, so it is worth doing this one shot at a time rather than using the multi-angle face workflows when using a portrait shot and you want the best character accuracy to build your character from. When its good QWEN rocks, but it can throw wobblers.
</br>

2. **SWAPPING PERSON IN IMAGE 1 WITH PERSON FROM IMAGE 2** 

- **I dont try to precisely maintain emotion or the position.** It doesnt really work. I prompt for accurate swap but with a whole new image using the contents. that works. It can stay localised e.g. only swapping the head or face if you prompt it as such, but it wont take on the emotion or the head direction of the original image.
</br>
- **The problem is that I also need this for full length body shots**. I do it by merging (compositing) the result back in to the full length body original image later (using Krita). The way to address the seems or issues is to run it through QWEN again using "relight" or tricks in Krita to upscale and fix seams. Its a bit of a journey for this part, and everyone will have their approach.

work with it like that and its really good. try to do other things and you can end up frustrated. AI do be like that.

---

# NOTES ON SWAPPING

- trying to match the emotion doesnt seem to work so well. easier to let it straight swap the heads.

- use "relight" in the prompt if you want to apply some relighting it is now built into the QWEN 2511 image edit model

- head size changes occur so trying to push it into a particular image can end up with odd proportions compared to original. For this reason I use this mainly for portrait close up shots of people to create characters.


## EXAMPLE PROMPTS:

### 1 IMAGE INPUT:

`turn the man's head so he is looking straight at the viewer`

### 2 IMAGE INPUT:

`headswap the two people. the final image should be a man in white t-shirt.`
headswap the two men. the final image should be one person, who looks like man from image 2.
